An effect can confine itself to one owner's cells (rich-effects-cbgp.4y4) (#394)

* An effect can confine itself to one owner's cells (rich-effects-cbgp.4y4)

EffectCell carries the cell's anchor, and confined(effect, owner) applies an
effect only to the cells that owner drew. Strip and FlexStrip stamp every item's
cells with the item (drawItem), and CellJoiner stamps each join cell inked in a
neighbour's colour with that neighbour, so a seam's arrow moves with the item it
points out of; a cell inked in a role or a mix stays the join's alone.

The effects-feel demo's pulse now singles out its items by owner instead of by
fill hex.

* A seam cell owns its ink and its ground separately (rich-effects-cbgp.4y4)

A powerline arrow is inked in the fill it points out of over the fill it
points into, so stamping the whole cell with one neighbour left the other
item's colour moving with it and the owner's own ground still. CellJoiner
now records, per cell, whose colour its ink and its ground show
(colorsOwnedBy), and confined moves only the owner's sides. Join cells no
longer borrow an item's anchor at a join-relative column, so hit-testing
and the anchor's position stay true.

* Say which owners confined can reach; pulsedOn names both arrows (rich-effects-cbgp.4y4)
Whole-keys settle reads a chunk's rest in full when a sink throws mid-drain (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Whole-keys settle: ESC [ / ESC O is the Alt chord; settling survives a throwing sink (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Review fixes: whole-keys feed no longer runs the split hold logic; header
names InputChunks; docs Input field typed; integration test that a
NodeTerminalHost in the docs worker reads whole-keys. Split-host residue
filed as rich-host-input-gnl7.

A whole-keys host settles each input chunk; no lone ESC is held for a timer (rich-host-input-ab9n)

TerminalHost declares inputChunks: xterm.js (BrowserTerminalHost, and the
docs worker's simulated stdin through NodeTerminalHost) never splits a key
across chunks, so an ESC left at a chunk's end is Escape and what followed
it is re-read. A tty stays "split" and keeps the setTimeout(0) hold.
